She Doesn't
Sell Art.
She Solves
Space.

Julia S. Rasor spent thirty years inventing machines that keep human bodies running, then brought that precision to the human form. Today she builds monumental bronze for landscape architects, estate architects, interior designers, and corporate art curators who need a statement piece engineered for its site.

“I won't let it exist unless it's a head-turner, a statement piece where people have to do a double-take.”

She isn't waiting in a gallery to be discovered. She's a subcontractor you commission and build with, like any specialist whose work has to hold up under real demands.

Collaboration Protocol — 04

A Business
Partner,
Not a Wildcard

Before sculpture, Rasor ran companies, and she still runs every commission the same way: on scope, on schedule, no surprises.

See the Devotion Behind the Discipline

She raised venture capital, holds more than 30 patents, and spent three decades directing product development and clinical research across more than 60 medical devices and 100-plus clinical trials. Her inventions include ECHOVIST, the first commercial ultrasound contrast agent. She knows blueprints, timelines, and budgets, because for thirty years, that was the job. She treats a sculpture brief the way she once treated a device spec.

Structural Portals & Spatial Anchors — 05

Site-responsive works and commissions for landscape environments, architectural spaces, luxury entrances, and refined interiors.

Lead Series

The Architecture Series

Her most recent, most site-ready body of work draws from mid-century Modernism and Brutalism: raw, angular forms with the discipline of an engineering drawing, built to stand alongside concrete, steel, and glass.

Supporting Series

The Fashion Series

A second collection, drawn from her avant-garde Fashion series, brings runway figures caught between one stride and the next, for spaces that call for movement instead of mass.

Both are commissioned, sited, and installed, not simply set down.
Physics of Integration — 06

Built to Mount,
not just
to Look At

Every custom gate, portal, entryway, or interior anchor solves one hard problem: how do you attach a massive bronze figure to steel or concrete without an on-site welding operation that damages both metals? Rasor's answer is a pin-and-gravity mounting system, no bronze-to-steel welding required.

See How It's Engineered

Precision steel pins, welded into the gate or base, hold the bronze piece in place by its own weight when it drops onto them. The install is clean, secure, and reversible if a piece ever needs to move. That precision comes from a career spent engineering artificial heart assist devices, where she learned exactly how weight, balance, and load move through a structure built to bear real physical stress.

Volumetric Scalability — 07

One Original. Any Scale.

Long before she sculpted, Rasor used 3D scanning to prototype medical devices. She uses the same technology now, scanning and archiving every original so it can be reproduced at any scale, in any material, from a four-inch bronze pendant to an eight-and-a-half-foot outdoor monument.

Commission a courtyard-scale bronze, and she can deliver a matching four-inch reproduction alongside it: a closing gift for the client the sculpture was built for.

One Discipline, Not Two — 08

One
Discipline,
Not Two

“Art and science are not separate domains but collaborative engines for innovation, creativity, and progress throughout human history.”
— Julia S. Rasor

She never trained at art school. She approaches sculpture the way she approached invention: the trial and error of a scientist, testing polystyrene, steel mesh, concrete, and cast-off materials until the form holds. Her father, Ned S. Rasor, PhD, raised her in a household where invention wasn't remarkable, it was simply how you engaged with the world. Years later, she co-invented several of her own patents alongside him, then carried that same instinct into bronze.
